topic: Kubernetes YAML manifest structure — all key fields
linkedin_hook: Mastering Kubernetes YAML manifests just got easier with this ultimate cheatsheet!
linkedin_intro: As a senior DevOps engineer, I've worked with numerous Kubernetes deployments and I've compiled a list of essential YAML manifest structures to help you streamline your workflow. This cheatsheet is based on my real-world experience and is designed to be a practical resource for DevOps engineers. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced practitioner, this cheatsheet will help you navigate the complex world of Kubernetes YAML manifests.

items.command:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: example-pod
items.description: Defines a basic pod with the specified name

items.command:
spec:
  containers:
  - name: example-container
    image: example-image
items.description: Specifies a container with the given name and image
Exposes a port from the container
Sets an environment variable for the container
Mounts a volume to the specified path in the container

items.command:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-deployment
items.description: Defines a basic deployment with the specified name

items.command:
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-app
items.description: Specifies the number of replicas and the label selector

items.command:
template:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: example-app
  spec:
    containers:
    - name: example-container
      image: example-image
items.description: Defines the pod template for the deployment

items.command:
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 0
items.description: Specifies the rolling update strategy for the deployment
Specifies the minimum number of seconds a pod must be ready before it is considered available

items.command:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: example-service
items.description: Defines a basic service with the specified name

items.command:
spec:
  selector:
    app: example-app
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: 80
items.description: Specifies the label selector and the port configuration
Exposes the service as a load balancer
Specifies the IP address of the load balancer
Specifies the external traffic policy for the service

items.command:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: example-pv
items.description: Defines a basic persistent volume with the specified name
Specifies the capacity and access modes of the persistent volume
Specifies the reclaim policy for the persistent volume
Specifies the local path for the persistent volume
Specifies the storage class for the persistent volume

items.command:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: example-config-map
items.description: Defines a basic config map with the specified name
Specifies a key-value pair for the config map
Specifies a binary key-value pair for the config map
Specifies that the config map is immutable
Specifies the config map name as a label

pro_tips: Use the `kubectl explain` command to get detailed information about a specific field in a YAML manifest, for example: `kubectl explain pod.spec.containers`
Use the `kubectl apply` command with the `--validate` flag to validate a YAML manifest without applying it, for example: `kubectl apply --validate -f example.yaml`
Use the `kubectl rollout` command to manage rollouts of deployments, for example: `kubectl rollout status deployment/example-deployment`
Use the `kubectl get` command with the `--output` flag to customize the output format, for example: `kubectl get pods --output=jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}'`
